title: Ozone depletion from CFC hypothesis and long-term monitoring to Montreal Protocol controls
pressure: Useful stable CFCs appeared capable of transporting chlorine to the stratosphere and depleting protective ozone; the hypothesized global harm was difficult to observe directly.
preExistingWorldModel: CFC industrial use was widespread; ozone chemistry and Dobson monitoring existed, but models/measurements were uncertain and Antarctic depletion was not recognized.
candidateRoutes: continue CFC use pending direct damage
observationsAndInstruments: Molina/Rowland warned in 1974 that CFCs could damage ozone.
Monitoring/research expanded while national measures differed.
Long-running BAS measurements revealed dramatic Antarctic spring ozone loss in 1985.
Vienna created a cooperation framework; the 1987 Montreal Protocol imposed controls and was strengthened as evidence/alternatives improved.
decisiveTests: connect emissions to stratospheric chlorine/ozone consequences
independent measurements distinguish real depletion from instrument/data artifact
controls remain feasible across countries/industries and adapt as evidence/substitutes change
technicalOrScientificTransition: Ozone protection coupled hypothesis, long-horizon observation, independent confirmation, substitute technology and adaptive international control; neither one paper nor one treaty explains the correction.
rivalsAndFailures: A locally useful stable chemical created a delayed global externality.
The strongest empirical signal appeared after the causal hypothesis.
Treaty commitments changed as science and substitute availability changed.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: Ozone protection coupled hypothesis, long-horizon observation, independent confirmation, substitute technology and adaptive international control; neither one paper nor one treaty explains the correction.
sourceNativeSummary: Ozone protection coupled hypothesis, long-horizon observation, independent confirmation, substitute technology and adaptive international control; neither one paper nor one treaty explains the correction.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement most constrained diffusion at each lifecycle phase?
